chunks: Al-Shalmaghani narrated in the Book of the Successors: Abu Ja'far al-Marwazi said:

Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umar and a group went to al-Askar and witnessed the days of Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him) while he was alive. Among them was Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Tanin. Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Umar wrote asking permission to enter the tomb. Ali ibn Ahmad said to him, 'Do not write my name, for I do not seek permission.' So he did not write his name, and the reply came to Ja'far, 'Enter you and the one who did not seek permission.'

key_terms.أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ: Abu Muhammad, a title for Imam Hasan al-Askari (a.s.)
key_terms.الْعَسْكَر: Al-Askar, the district in Samarra where the Imams resided and were buried
key_terms.الْقَبْر: The tomb, referring to the Imam's burial place

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Tanin entering the tomb of Imam al-Askari?
ai.summary: This narrative from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* illustrates the social dynamics and spiritual status of companions during the Minor Occultation, specifically highlighting the humility of Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Tanin. His refusal to seek formal permission for entry into the Imam's tomb, resulting in his inclusion with those who did, underscores the Shia emphasis on modesty and divine favor in the presence of the Imam. This incident serves as a practical example of *adab* (etiquette) and the subtle signs of piety recognized by the Imamate.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: 293- It is narrated from Shalmaghani in Awsiya that Abu Ja’far Marwazi narrated that:

Ja’far Ibn Muhammad Ibn Umar and a number of others came to Askar and were present there during the time Imam Hasan Askari (a.s) was alive. Amongst them was Ali Ibn Ahmad Ibn Tanin. Ja’far Ibn Muhammad Ibn Umar wrote a letter asking permission to enter the tomb. Ali Ibn Ahmad said to him, “Do not write my name. I am not seeking permission.” Ja’far Ibn Muhammad did not write his name and the reply came, “Enter you and the one who did not seek permission.”
